messages:
ella: Heads-up: enterprise-prod customer (DataCorp) wants a contract addendum: 99.9% p99 latency SLO for text-generation endpoints on Dedicated. Need product/eng sync to scope PRD + acceptance criteria. Is this feasible?
jun: Can you paste the exact ask? p99 99.9 is very tight depending on seq len.
ella: Quote from their email: 'p99 <= 800ms for sequences <= 512 tokens; error budget 0.1% monthly; automatic fallback to hosted variant allowed but must be labeled and tracked.'
liam: We should separate latency SLO vs availability SLA. They want error budget 0.1% — essentially 99.9% availability. For our current Dedicated baseline p99 is ~600ms for short seq on A100s, but tail events >2s exist.
sarah: If we promise p99 800ms, need canary traffic and warmed KV caches + reserved burst capacity. Also need fallback policy: degrade to a quantized model variant with quality guardrails.
mike: Quality guardrails need acceptance tests: evals on their sample prompt set and a human review threshold. Who owns evals?
anya: Growth/CS will manage contractual side. For the PRD: include acceptance criteria: measured on production traffic for 2 weeks with canary, <0.1% infra errors, rollback triggers, and clear observability. Also rollout steps and monitoring dashboards.
jun: Edge case: sequence >512 tokens. Spec should define behavior: either reject with 413 or route to a 'long-seq' SLA with different SLO. Need to confirm with legal/customer.
liam: Agree. Also consider region affinity: DataCorp runs in eu-west. Need multi-region capacity or explicit regional SLO.
ella: Draft PRD notes I'm adding: SLO targets, error budget policy, fallback model list, canary plan, acceptance eval suite, test dataset, rollback triggers, billing delta. Anything missing?
sarah: Add performance isolation: pin GPUs to avoid noisy neighbors for Dedicated customer pools. Also explicit KB around KV cache warmup windows.
anya: Also add contract language about 'graceful degradation'—must notify customer and provide per-incident postmortem within SLA.
mike: On implementation: runtime needs to support per-customer routing policy with priority queue and preemption. Eng-runtime team: can we prototype with tenant tags and warm replicas?
jun: We can do priority tagging and pre-warmed workers but preemption complexity is high. Estimate 3 sprints to land baseline + canary infra.
liam: :thumbsup: Add cost estimate: ~2.5x baseline GPU footprint for 99.9 p99 with pre-warm and reserved capacity. That will change pricing.
ella: Action items: @jun draft technical RFC with perf baseline + pre-warm plan by Fri. @mike draft eval checklist + sample dataset. @anya coordinate customer expectations and contract text. @liam produce cost delta. We'll sync Tues.
ops-bot: New task created: SLO-enterprise-datacorp (#3297) assigned to jun, due 2026-04-10.
anya: One more thing: acceptance criteria must include 'no silent quality regressions' — tie to Redwood Optimize monitors and enable regression alerts.
jun: Noted. I'll include performance SLIs (p50/p95/p99), error rate, queue length, KV cache hit rate, and model output quality metrics.
mike: Example canary config:
```
canary:
  percent: 5
  duration: 14d
  metrics: [p99_latency, error_rate, quality_regressions]
```
ella: Thanks. I'll spin up initial PRD doc in product-drive and link in this thread once draft ready.
